quarterly_data.signal: Segment results for the year ended March 2026 (annual securities report): consolidated revenue JPY 10,063.2 billion (prior year JPY 8,695.5 billion) and business profit JPY 514.1 billion (prior JPY 683.2 billion); the Steelmaking segment is about 90% of consolidated revenue. Steelmaking revenue JPY 9,221.7 billion (JPY 7,874.3 billion), segment profit JPY 439.9 billion (JPY 621.0 billion); Engineering revenue JPY 394.4 billion (JPY 400.4 billion), profit JPY 23.1 billion (JPY 14.6 billion); Chemicals & Materials revenue JPY 257.9 billion (JPY 269.1 billion), profit JPY 21.9 billion (JPY 18.9 billion); System Solutions revenue JPY 382.8 billion (JPY 339.3 billion), profit JPY 43.3 billion (JPY 38.8 billion). The JPY 181.0 billion fall in Steelmaking profit: production / shipment volume -JPY 20.0 billion, margin (incl. FX) -JPY 115.0 billion, cost improvement +JPY 130.0 billion, the parent's own overseas business -JPY 35.0 billion, raw-materials business -JPY 71.0 billion, group steel companies -JPY 35.0 billion, inventory valuation -JPY 9.0 billion, other -JPY 26.0 billion. Export sales (including overseas subsidiaries' local sales) were JPY 5,203,069 million, 51.7% of sales (prior JPY 3,585,755 million, 41.2%); by destination North America 38.5% (13.9%), Asia 35.5% (57.9%), Europe 12.6% (9.6%). quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Steel annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 2030 Medium- to Long-Term Management Plan (published December 2025; annual securities report): by fiscal 2030 (the year ending March 2031) the company targets consolidated underlying profit of JPY 1 trillion or more per year and ROE of around 10%, and aims in future for global crude steel output of 100 million tonnes or more. It plans about JPY 6 trillion of capital and business investment over the five years from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2030 (April 2026 to March 2031), including about US$11 billion of investment in U.S. Steel through end-2028. Overseas focus regions are the US / Europe, India and Thailand: in India, ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India will expand capacity at the Hazira steelworks, including state-of-the-art flat-steel facilities already under way, and start building an integrated steelworks in the south (Rajayapeta, Andhra Pradesh); in Thailand the company holds about 30% of the flat-steel market through G Steel, G J Steel and NS-Siam United Steel. In Japan it will idle one continuous annealing line at East Nippon Works Kashima around the end of fiscal 2027 (March 2028) as part of optimising production, and aims to implement large electric arc furnaces by 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: Fiscal 2030 (year ending March 2031) targets: underlying profit JPY 1 trillion or more per year; ROE around 10%; about JPY 6 trillion investment over five years (incl. about US$11 billion in U.S. Steel through end-2028)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Steel annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Electrical steel and capacity (annual securities report): under the 2030 plan the company is increasing electrical steel sheet capacity at Kyushu Works Yawata, Setouchi Works Hirohata and the Hanshin area (Sakai), alongside using the Nagoya Works next-generation hot strip mill, to capture domestic demand. With the U.S. Steel merger (acquired June 18, 2025, 100% of voting rights) the group's global crude steel production capacity expanded to 82 million tonnes; the company says it will offer products and services drawing on Nippon Steel's and U.S. Steel's technology in high-grade products such as electrical steel sheets and automotive steel sheets.
quarterly_data.figure: Global crude steel capacity 82 million tonnes after the U.S. Steel merger; electrical steel capacity expansion at Yawata, Hirohata and Sakai (no amount stated)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Steel annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capex and planned facilities (annual securities report): capital expenditure in the year ended March 2026 was JPY 942,986 million (+62%), of which Steelmaking JPY 935,057 million (+64%). Over the five years fiscal 2021-2025 (April 2021 to March 2026) capex totalled about JPY 3.5 trillion and business investment about JPY 4.0 trillion, both including U.S. Steel-related investment. Major planned facilities: Nagoya Works (Tokai, Aichi) next-generation hot strip mill, total JPY 270.0 billion, started May 2022, completion in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 (April-June 2026), capacity 6 million t/year; Kyushu Works (Kitakyushu) electric arc furnace (new), total JPY 630.2 billion, started May 2025, completion in the second half of fiscal 2029 (October 2029-March 2030), 2 million t/year; Setouchi Works (Himeji) electric arc furnace (expansion), total JPY 140.0 billion, started May 2025, completion in the second half of fiscal 2029 (October 2029-March 2030), 0.5 million t/year; East Nippon Works (Kimitsu) No. 3 coke oven (revamp), total JPY 39.0 billion, completion in the first half of fiscal 2026 (April-September 2026), 0.7 million t/year; Yamaguchi Works (Shunan) electric arc furnace (revamp), total JPY 98.5 billion, completion in the second half of fiscal 2028 (October 2028-March 2029), 0.4 million t/year. The shift from blast furnaces to electric arc furnaces was selected for support under Japan's GX Promotion Act in May 2025. Investment amounts for the next fiscal year are still being formulated.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 942,986 million (+62%); Nagoya hot strip mill JPY 270.0 billion (6 million t/year, April-June 2026); Kyushu EAF JPY 630.2 billion (2 million t/year, October 2029-March 2030)

quarterly_data.signal: Chemicals & Materials and AI demand (annual securities report): at Nippon Steel Chemical & Material, functional materials revenue rose to JPY 115.0 billion (prior JPY 100.0 billion) as functional resins, substrate materials and semiconductor materials performed well on growing demand for AI servers and data centers; coal chemicals fell to JPY 52.0 billion (JPY 61.0 billion) on weak demand for needle coke for graphite electrodes, and chemicals to JPY 91.0 billion (JPY 108.0 billion) on weak benzene and styrene monomer markets. quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Steel annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management's view (annual securities report): management states that apart from some fields such as AI, power and defense, base demand from manufacturing and construction stayed weak in Japan and overseas and the global steel business environment remains critical, with China's continued overproduction and cheap exports depressing international prices. It expects growth from emerging economies and expanding AI- and energy-related investment, rising steel demand in India and higher demand for high-grade steel from manufacturing reshoring in the US, but continued decline in Japanese demand; it expects resolving the global steel oversupply to take time and the tough environment to continue. For fiscal 2026 (April 2026 to March 2027) it says it cannot yet comprehensively and reasonably assess the impact of the Middle East situation on its results. Management states that its structural measures have built an advantage that can secure underlying consolidated business profit of JPY 600 billion or more even as demand falls and competition intensifies.
quarterly_data.figure: Underlying consolidated business profit of JPY 600 billion or more secured by structural measures (company statement)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Steel annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D and new products (annual securities report): group R&D spending was JPY 82.7 billion (Steelmaking JPY 70.7 billion, Engineering JPY 3.0 billion, Chemicals & Materials JPY 5.2 billion, System Solutions JPY 3.7 billion). Developments: a high-bendability 2.0 GPa-class hot-stamping steel developed with Mazda was adopted, in what the company calls a world first, for the front bumper reinforcement of the new CX-5; sales of Alloy825 (UNS N08825) nickel corrosion-resistant alloy plate began in January 2026; for the high-strength NSYP385B HYPER BEAM, MEGA HYPER BEAM sizes were added in April 2025, raising the production series from 19 to 49, with wider adoption expected in large logistics facilities, high-rises and data centers; blast-furnace hydrogen reduction tests cut CO2 emissions by 43% in 2024 (a world first, per the company) and reached 45% by March 2026. Engineering R&D covers waste-to-energy plants, cogeneration, carbon recycling and offshore wind power facilities.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D JPY 82.7 billion (Steelmaking JPY 70.7 billion); 2.0 GPa hot-stamping steel; HYPER BEAM series 19 to 49; CO2 cut 45%

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Steel annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Material contracts and restructuring (annual securities report): on February 5, 2026 subsidiary Nippon Steel Engineering signed a basic memorandum with Kanadevia to study a business integration, with a final agreement planned for September 2026 and an effective date planned for April 2027, by an absorption merger with Kanadevia as the surviving company; the combined company is to remain listed on the TSE Prime market and may become a listed affiliate or subsidiary of Nippon Steel. Nippon Steel will absorb its wholly owned subsidiary Sanyo Special Steel effective April 1, 2027 (contract of May 13, 2026). Ended during the year: the US joint venture with ArcelorMittal (AM/NS Calvert) on June 18, 2025 through the NS Kote share transfer; the global strategic alliance with ArcelorMittal on March 27, 2026; and the USIMINAS shareholders' agreement on February 10, 2026 after the shares were transferred to Ternium Investments. Under the June 13, 2025 national security agreement with the US government, Nippon Steel committed to invest about US$11 billion in U.S. Steel by 2028, including initial investment in a greenfield project to be completed after 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: Engineering-Kanadevia integration planned effective April 2027; Sanyo Special Steel merger effective April 1, 2027; about US$11 billion U.S. Steel investment by 2028
